summary_rationale: Uber remains a high-cash-conversion, dual-engine global marketplace compounder, though its mid-2026 M&A pivot and balance-sheet complexity require disciplined monitoring. Through Q3 2026, MAPCs reached 215M (+14% YoY), trips reached 4,061M (+16% YoY), Gross Bookings compounded +20% YoY to $59.82B (Q4 guided $63.25B–$65.25B), 9M 2026 GAAP Operating Income rose +39% YoY to $5,260M, and Free Cash Flow hit $7,613M in 9M 2026 ($10.42B TTM, >100% Adjusted EBITDA conversion on 0.6% capex intensity). Uber One (>50M members) and Advertising (>$2.5B run-rate) continue strengthening unit retention. kpi_health is PASS_WITH_WATCH across five material risks surfaced in Q3 2026 filings: (1) autonomous disintermediation and partner take-rate compression as Waymo runs a competing first-party app alongside Uber and Tesla/Zoox scale; (2) major capital-allocation pivot toward $14.8B Delivery Hero SE and $2.3B ezCater pending M&A (on top of $5.5B deployed in 9M 2026 M&A/TRS), lifting long-term debt +49% to $15,664M ($15,787M principal) and slowing buybacks; (3) $13,709M insurance reserves requiring $11,372M of restricted cash/investments; (4) UK HMRC $3.4B (£2.6B) back-VAT dispute ($1.5B pending cash appeal outflow), Nov 2026 Australia payroll tax ruling, and active FTC scrutiny on Uber One and algorithmic pricing; and (5) Delivery incremental margin friction against DoorDash/Instacart alongside persistently loss-making Freight ($(33)M Q3 loss).
